bench.rule: no hardware measurement claim without hardware

claim_boundary: Static sidecar artifact. No hardware measurement.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: Prefill / multi-token (different x per row) does not collapse and needs a different kernel. Occupancy vs bytes is the live wall, not gather-vs-sequential (NS-032).
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Do not rerun the B-sweep of ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH as if it were new. Falsify the FUSED remainder: a kernel that keeps x resident and reads packed rows vs the existing per-expert qwen80_routed_expert_wave_gate_up dispatches, on the same packed payload, under a protected lease (later lane). Kill if the fused wave matches the independent-dispatch complete-token within noise.
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: None by itself (payloads unchanged). Byte effect is UNKNOWN/none unless packed layout also changes.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Removes k independent loads of x and k separate gate/up launches. Magnitude UNKNOWN; stacked-dense cousin was marginal at decode top-k in ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH.
compute_candidates.mechanism: one hidden vector entering many experts: keep x register/SRAM resident and stream selected expert rows against it in one wave, fused with SiLU(gate)*up. Not a stacked dense table of independent W_e.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: Load x once into threadgroup memory. Each threadgroup owns an intermediate row of a selected expert's packed gate/up and dots against resident x. Packed values are consumed in-register. No dense W_e, no stacked dense table.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: k independent (gate_proj x) and (up_proj x) against the same x, plus k independent loads of x.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not naive expert-table batching (already measured). Not a trivial shared basis (no shared W).
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source stores one matrix per expert and the runtime honors that independence with one dispatch family per expert, even though the activation is identical.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: Decode routes one token to k experts and every one multiplies THE SAME activation. ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH already showed that stacking independent W_e against shared x IS a taller matvec (exact 0.0 residual) and that at realistic decode top-k the representation-native stacked path is at best marginal. The untested remainder is fused register-resident x with packed payloads and organ fusion, without forming a stacked dense table.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: If B does not capture XX^T, quality dies before compute pays. Skinny maps that are not actually skinny (r ~ d_in) are a compute loss (extra round trip).
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Same cheapest falsifier as shared input transforms (uncoded V, real X). Kill on function before claiming a compute win. A protected complete-token comparison is a later lane.
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Follows the paired storage candidate; may be ~0 if B is stored in addition to W. UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Replaces k full matvecs with 1 wide + k skinny. Algebraic reduction only; ns UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.mechanism: shared xB transform with small expert-specific transforms: z = x @ B once; y_e = z @ C_e. Compute dual of shared input / common right.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: One GEMV z = B @ x in SRAM. Selected C_e stream against z. No W_e = C_e B. Gate and up may share the same z.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: Each selected expert applies its own full input projection to x.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not trivial shared basis (B is a transform of x, not a shared W). Not ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH stacking of independent W_e.
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source matrices B_e are independent, so the compiler has no license to hoist a common transform of x.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: If a shared B exists (activation-PCA or joint right factor), the repeated full matvec is almost entirely duplicated work on x. This is the execution of STORE-SHARED-INPUT-TRANSFORM / STORE-COMMON-RIGHT-SUBSPACE, listed on the compute axis because the win can be FLOPs even when stored bytes barely move.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: Forcing a shared U so this identity applies can be a capability regression. Do not apply the identity when U is not shared.
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Identity check: shared-U expand-then-sum vs reduce-then-expand must match at 0.0 residual (planted). Kill the candidate if a real organ requires per-expert U to meet the function screen (then the identity does not apply).
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: None extra; depends on storing shared U. UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Cuts k-1 expansions of size d_model. ns UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.mechanism: latent weighted reduction: apply router weights in a small latent and reduce there, instead of weighting full d_model outputs.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: Each selected expert writes an r-vector. Weighted sum in r. One U @ u. Exact when U is shared. No dense down_proj.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: k independent down_proj expansions to d_model, then a weighted sum in d_model.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not expert merging (all selected experts still run). Not mean subtraction.
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source down_proj is per-expert to full hidden, so the combiner is written after expansion.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: The combiner is linear. If experts emit aligned latents, sum_e π_e (U u_e) = U (sum_e π_e u_e). The reduction moves before the expansion. This is free algebra when U is shared; it is the compute reason to want STORE-SHARED-OUTPUT-LATENT.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: down_proj is tolerant relative to gate, not invulnerable. A single U can smear expert-specific output directions.
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Planted shared-U identity (must be exact). Then one-layer down function screen vs per-expert U. Kill if per-expert U is required.
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: k down payloads collapse to one U plus skinny latents if storage follows. UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.mechanism: one output expansion: a single shared expansion of a reduced intermediate, rather than k independent down_proj GEMVs.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind one U. Consume the reduced latent. One GEMV to d_model. Never k packed down_proj payloads applied independently unless the function screen forbids sharing U.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not a trivial shared basis of whole W. Not same-index tying.
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source has one down_proj per expert; the runtime launches them as independent organs.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: Same algebra as latent weighted reduction, named separately because the repeated work is the expansion itself even when weights are applied after. Shared U is the storage partner.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: Large codebook gathers are dead. A shared decode that is the raw-PQ family at one bit will collapse on a real forward. Organ split still applies.
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if K is large enough to become a gather LUT (dead lever: learned codebook LUT). Kill if the kernel writes or caches a dense W (NS-018: caching decoded W restores the footprint the representation exists to remove). Kill if the codebook is raw-weight PQ at ~1 BPW (dead family). A planted tiny shared CB plus fused FMA must beat per-expert unpack on a synthetic packed payload before any specimen is touched.
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Codebook amortized; payloads are indices. Magnitude UNKNOWN. Raw-weight 1-bit PQ is dead; this does not reopen it.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Removes per-expert unpack prologues. ns UNKNOWN. Reconstruction penalty is vehicle-specific (NNS-011); do not cite a measured factor here.
compute_candidates.mechanism: shared representation decode: a tiny shared codebook / scale family lives in registers; per-expert payloads are indices consumed fused with the matvec. Decode is not a per-expert prologue that writes dense W.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: Codebook in registers (K tiny). Fused FMA of codebook entries with x. No densify-then-GEMM. Organ-specific codebooks allowed.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: Per-expert dequant / unpack / scale application before or during each expert matvec.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not NS-010 unconditioned shared codebook on raw routed-expert weights. Not entropy-coded Lloyd indices. Not NS-018 cache-decoded-W. Not NNS-018 single-family-across-organs (organ-specific tiny CBs are allowed).
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source payloads were packed independently, so decode is written as an expert-local prologue rather than a bank-level codebook in registers.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: Independent per-expert unpack + scale is repeated work on the same code family. Atlas large-LUT and entropy-coded Lloyd indices are dead; tiny lookup-free shared CB is the remaining decode-sharing object. NS-012 / NNS-018 forbid assuming one family across organs, so codebooks stay organ-tagged.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: NNS-018 / uniform-subbit: organs do not fail together. Sharing V across gate and up can kill gate to save a projection that down never needed. Islands may have to keep gate independent.
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if a shared V for gate+up fails the function screen on gate (dominant_failure_organ historically). The fused-but-unshared kernel is the control, not a missing fusion.
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: May cut stored input factors if V is shared; UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One shared input GEMV for two organs instead of two. ns UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.mechanism: shared projections across organs: hoist a common transform of x that both gate and up (and possibly the shared expert) can reuse, instead of two independent input projections per expert.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: One V @ x. Skinny gate core and skinny up core against z, fused SiLU product. Independent per-organ paths remain legal for the sensitive organ (gate). No densified W_gate or W_up.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: gate_proj @ x and up_proj @ x as two full projections, even when fused in one kernel.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not already-built fused gate-up (that still uses two matrices). Not a trivial shared basis of the whole expert.
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source has two independent matrices per expert; fusion multiplies both by x but does not hoist a shared factor.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: Per-expert fused gate-up already exists (qwen80_routed_expert_wave_gate_up dots gate and up against x in one kernel). That is fusion, not sharing: the two matrices are still independent. The untested share is a common right factor across gate and up, so z = V @ x serves both organs.

compute_candidates.capability_risk: A large residual update (attention + MLP) can make Δ as expensive as x, so reuse does not pay. Do not reopen weight tying to make the adapter look good.
compute_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if ||V @ x_{L+1} - adapter(z_L)|| is not smaller than ||V @ x_{L+1}|| on a real residual stream (then reuse is a no-op). Do not score by W cosine across layers (dead tying metric).
compute_candidates.expected_byte_effect: May let V be stored per-block instead of per-layer. UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Avoids a full V @ x at L+1 when Δ is cheap. ns UNKNOWN.
compute_candidates.mechanism: cross-layer reused transforms: reuse a transform of the residual stream (V_L @ x_L) as an initialization for layer L+1, with a small adapter, instead of independently projecting at every layer.
compute_candidates.native_execution_concept: Keep z_L = V @ x_L. At L+1 compute z_{L+1} = z_L + V @ Δ (or a small adapter on z_L). Token path uses z, never W. V may be per-block (storage SB9) or per-layer with reuse of the product.
compute_candidates.repeated_computation: Independent V_L @ x_L at every layer, including when x_L is a small residual update of x_{L-1}.
compute_candidates.scar_distance: Not same-index cross-layer weight tying. Not an unchanged archetype copied across layers.
compute_candidates.why_currently_repeated: Source layers are separate tensors with no residual-product identity expressed in the graph, so each layer projects x from scratch.
compute_candidates.why_it_might_work: Layers are independent modules in source, but x_{L+1} is a residual update of x_L, so V @ x_{L+1} ≈ V @ x_L + V @ Δ. Same-index WEIGHT tying is dead; reusing the TRANSFORM of x is a compute hoist, not a W template. SB9 in the shared-basis packet was table-trim of V across a block, not this compute reuse.

killed_hypotheses.scope: MODEL_SPECIFIC on Q80/F0/F1; DSV4F pairwise cosine is still unmeasured
killed_hypotheses.title: raw global expert similarity
killed_hypotheses.why_dead: Q80 L10 n=96: gate pairwise cosine mean 0.00414, up ~0; top-32 right-subspace overlap 0.025/0.020; k90=84/96. Qwen3-30B-A3B L2 n=32: mean cosine 0.0024/5.6e-5/-1e-6; subtracting the mean expert leaves residual norm 0.984. Foundry atlas inter_expert_redundancy: mean pairwise cosine 1e-4. NS-010 / NNS-004: shared cross-expert basis/codebook/template is REFUTED on Q80/F0/F1.

killed_hypotheses.reopen_condition: Never as an unconditioned weight-space shared basis on Q80/Qwen3.8. A one-sided, clustered, route-conditioned, or activation-PCA object is a different hypothesis and is not this scar.
killed_hypotheses.scope: unconditioned weight-space shared basis / shared codebook
killed_hypotheses.title: trivial shared basis
killed_hypotheses.why_dead: C1SHAREDBASIS_DESIGN: sharing lost on FIDELITY, not because a kernel rematerialized dense W (associativity identity holds). Verdict NOT_WORTH_BUILDING. SHARED_BASIS_COHERENT: no coherent shared-basis point beats q2f on both density and ns (died_at=held_out_activation). Flash bounded slice: shared bf16 basis + nf4 residual was 256000 bytes vs independent q4 174080 bytes (not smaller). NNS-004 / NS-010 kill the unconditioned shared-basis/codebook family on Q80.

killed_hypotheses.reopen_condition: Never as an unchanged template / same-index weight tie on the measured parents. A route-conditioned or residual-adapted archetype is a different hypothesis.
killed_hypotheses.scope: unchanged templates and same-index weight tying
killed_hypotheses.title: unchanged archetype
killed_hypotheses.why_dead: Foundry atlas cross_expert_and_cross_layer_tying: best single shared template explains 0.2513 of 4 experts' energy against an orthogonal null of exactly 0.2500; same-index cross-layer tying is indistinguishable from a different-index control at 1e-7. NNS-024: procedural / generated parameters (shared templates, same-index tying, generated expert bases) do not buy bits on mutually orthogonal experts. No file named flash_route_archetype_sparse_screen.py exists in this tree; the scar is the atlas/NNS template family.

native_execution_law: A kernel must consume factors / packed payloads / latents without rematerializing dense expert weights. Densify-then-GEMM is a fake share (C1SHAREDBASIS_DESIGN separated that failure from fidelity; fidelity still killed the trivial basis).

Did not take a hardware measurement; every expected effect is qualitative or algebraic. Complete-token ns, tps, and joules remain UNKNOWN.

recovered_implementation.not_duplicating: expert_family_genome.py and q80_cross_expert_structure.py MEASURE a specimen. shared-basis.md PROPOSES mechanisms in prose. Neither emits a sealed candidate catalog with compute-sharing as a first-class axis and a watched-fail scar guard. This module extends that science; it does not fork a second genome.
recovered_implementation.note: Naive expert sharing is already dead science. This module does not rerun it. Existing measurement tools fit specimens; this module generates unfitted structured candidates plus a scar guard. The named Flash doctor / route-conditioned / archetype screens are not in this tree.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If left spaces are as disjoint as Q80 right spaces, U captures noise and every expert loses the same complement. Gate is the historical first-break organ.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Instrument first on a planted U_shared @ C_e stack (must recover shared energy) and an orthogonal control (must not). Then, at a later funnel stage that owns a specimen, one layer / one organ / 8 experts: joint SVD of stacked W_e W_e^T energy in top-r. Kill if top-r energy is indistinguishable from the orthogonal null. Do not flatten-and-cosine. Do not fit the full bank in this lane.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Amortizes the wide output factor across E experts; per-expert payload shrinks to skinny C_e. Magnitude UNKNOWN pending specimen.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One shared expansion GEMV per token plus selected skinny maps. ns UNKNOWN (no GPU lease).
storage_candidates.mechanism: common left subspaces: share an output-side factor U across experts; keep expert-specific right factors C_e. Algebra y = U @ (C_e @ x) without forming W_e = U @ C_e.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind one U[d_model, r] per layer-organ and gathered C_e[r, d_in] for the selected experts. Compute z_e = C_e @ x (skinny), then y = U @ sum_e w_e z_e (or U @ z_e per expert if U is only partly shared). Never write W_e into DRAM.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not raw global similarity (does not flatten W or use pairwise cosine). Not a trivial shared basis (one-sided, not U_shared @ V_shared for all experts).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Q80's pairwise cosine kill is on flattened W, not on a joint SVD of the stacked left spaces. Left (output) subspaces were never the measured object in QWEN80_CROSS_EXPERT_STRUCTURE_NEGATIVE (that receipt reports right-subspace overlap of two experts). Geometry of down_proj is tall-output: sharing U amortizes the wide side.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: Q80 L10 pairwise right-overlap is already near null; a joint V may still exist and still be useless at the r that saves bytes. Do not treat a pairwise kill as this test, and do not treat a joint-V miss as a license to rerun flatten-and-cosine.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Planted shared-V stack vs orthogonal control (instrument). Then one-layer joint SVD of stacked W_e^T W_e. Kill if top-r energy matches the orthogonal null at the r the byte plan needs. Pairwise overlap of two experts is not this test.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Amortizes the wide input factor; payload is skinny C_e. Magnitude UNKNOWN. Q80 pairwise overlap 0.025 is a prior that this may die.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One shared V @ x plus selected skinny maps. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: common right subspaces: share an input-side factor V across experts in WEIGHT space of the stacked bank; expert-specific left cores C_e. Algebra y_e = C_e @ (V @ x).
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind one V[r, d_in] and gathered C_e[d_out, r]. Compute z = V @ x once per organ (or once per layer if gate/up share V), then y_e = C_e @ z. Never form W_e = C_e @ V.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not trivial shared basis (one-sided joint factor of the stack, not one unconditioned basis plus nf4 residual on raw W). Not activation-PCA (that is shared_input_transforms).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: A joint right factor of the expert STACK is a different object from pairwise top-32 overlap of expert 0 vs 1 (Q80 overlap 0.025 is a risk, not a joint-SVD kill). If a low-rank joint V exists, every selected expert reuses one V @ x.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If C_e must be nearly square at full rank, this is a byte loss (U,V plus cores exceed independent W). Capability follows the core rank: too-small C_e is a systematic, all-expert failure.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Planted sandwich recovers C_e energy; orthogonal W_e must force r ≈ min(d_out, d_in) to fit. Kill if the r that beats independent coding is not small enough to cut bytes after storing U and V once.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Payload per expert is C_e; U,V amortized over E. Win only if r is small. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Two shared GEMVs per token plus a tiny core GEMV per selected expert. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: expert-specific small cores: W_e ≈ U @ C_e @ V with C_e a small r x r (or r x s) core unique to the expert; U, V shared.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind U, V once and C_e for selected experts. Path: z = V @ x, u_e = C_e @ z, y_e = U @ u_e (or fused). Three GEMVs, none of which materializes W_e. C_e stays in registers if r is small.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not an unchanged archetype (the core changes per expert). Not a trivial shared basis (sandwich with a mixing core, not residual on a frozen shared W).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Orthogonality of flattened W does not forbid a shared sandwich with a mixing core. The core is the expert's identity; U and V are the bank's geometry. This is a parameterization, not a claim that experts look alike.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: Depth layers may have a flat expert-mode spectrum the way they have a flat Van Loan spectrum. Do not transfer the L0 Kronecker win to the bank, and do not transfer the depth Kronecker kill to the bank without measuring the expert mode.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Do not rerun single-tensor Kronecker at depth. Falsify the BANK decomposition: CP rank needed for a planted 3-way vs for real stack energy (later funnel). Kill if CP rank scales like E * min(d_out, d_in) (then there is no expert-mode structure).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: If the expert mode has low CP/Tucker rank, bytes scale as R*(E + d_out + d_in) not E*d_out*d_in. Magnitude UNKNOWN. L0 single-tensor Kronecker remaining live is a different object.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: R shared rank-1 (or Tucker) contractions instead of E independent matvecs. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: tensor decomposition of the expert BANK as a 3-way tensor (expert × out × in): CP / Tucker / tensor-train on the stack, consumed factor-wise.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Store CP atoms (a_r, u_r, v_r) or Tucker (G, A, U, V). Native: y = sum_r a_e,r * (u_r @ (v_r @ x)) or the Tucker contraction along in, then mix by expert row of A. Never reconstruct a dense slice W_e.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not NNS-016 (that is one expert tensor, Kronecker/TT/low-rank, layers >= 1). The expert index is an additional mode.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Single-tensor Kronecker of one expert at layers >= 1 is dead (flat Van Loan spectrum; NNS-016) with a named L0 exception. A 3-way decomposition of the bank can exist even when each slice is full-rank and pairwise cosine is ~0, because the expert mode is a new axis.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: Atlas expert-merging is DEAD (best survivor rel-err ~0.89-1.0). A cluster that silently becomes a merge will inherit that wall. Capability islands may not match cosine clusters.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if the K that beats the orthogonal null is ~E (then clustering is a rename of independent experts). Kill if the method reconstructs a held-out expert from cluster mates (that is dead expert-merging, atlas expert_merging_omitted_from_survivors / NNS-023).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: K shared wide factors plus skinny members. Win vs one-space only if K is small. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Up to min(K_selected, top-k) shared transforms per token. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: clustered subspaces: partition experts into K << E clusters; each cluster shares a left or right factor; members keep a skinny residual. All experts remain present.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind K shared factors and a cluster-id table (log2 K bits/expert). Selected expert e in cluster k uses V_k @ x then C_e. Gather V_k by cluster id, not by reconstructing W_e.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not raw global similarity (K spaces, not one). Not expert merging (every expert is stored; no omitted-expert reconstruction). Not an unchanged archetype (cluster factor plus member residual).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Global one-space sharing can fail while K cluster spaces succeed. Q80 k90=84/96 in expert-space energy says a SINGLE shared space needs almost E components; that does not bound K-way clustered spaces. This is not merging: omitted experts are not reconstructed.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: Raw-weight PQ/VQ at one bit collapsed on real forwards. Dictionary atoms that are just a PQ codebook on frozen W inherit that kill. Apple GPU large-LUT gather is also a dead lever.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if the K needed to hit a planted reconstruction is so large the dictionary plus codes exceed independent coding. Kill if atoms are applied by densifying W_e. Do not entropy-code Lloyd indices as the byte win (atlas entropy_coded_pq_indices).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Atoms amortized; per-expert payload is sparse codes. Win only at tiny K and lookup-free consume. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: nnz(e) atom applications per selected expert. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: dictionary families: a shared dictionary of linear atoms; each expert is a sparse combination of those atoms, executed as a sum of gathered low-rank factors.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Keep dictionary atoms as GEMM factors in registers/SRAM (tiny K). Expert e holds sparse indices and scales. y_e = sum_{k in supp(e)} s_{e,k} * (atom_k @ x). Lookup-free FMA. Never densify W_e from the atom sum. Large LUT gathers are a recorded dead lever.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not NS-010 unconditioned shared codebook on raw routed-expert weights. Not a single unchanged template. Not SB6-large-LUT.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: A single shared template is null (0.2513 vs 0.2500). A dictionary of many atoms with sparse codes can still span orthogonal experts the way a codebook spans orthogonal residuals, without claiming experts are similar. Source must not be raw-weight PQ (NS-raw-PQ dead at ~1 and ~0.49 BPW).

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If the router score does not predict the needed adaptation, this becomes the dead template with extra math. Over-mixing can smear capability across experts the router meant to keep distinct.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if g(π)=constant on held-out routes (then this collapses to the unchanged-archetype scar). Kill if mixing K archetypes cannot beat a single archetype by more than the orthogonal-null margin that already killed templates (0.0013 energy).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: K archetypes plus a conditioner instead of E full experts. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One conditioned mix plus the shared transform. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: route-conditioned archetypes: a small set of archetypal operators specialized by the live router score (or top-k identity), producing an adapted expert without storing a full W_e.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind K archetypal factors. Given router scores π, form a mixed core C(π) = sum_k g_k(π) C_k (or a sparse top-k mix) and apply C(π) @ (V @ x) natively. The kernel reads π and the archetypal factors; it does not write a dense adapted W.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not an unchanged archetype: the operator depends on the live route. The named Flash route-conditioned / archetype-sparse tools are absent from this tree; this candidate is the untested structured form, not a rerun of a missing screen.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Unchanged templates failed because they ignore the route. The router already computed a cheap score per expert; using that score as a conditioner is information the dead template threw away. Adaptation can be a scale, a mixing of K archetypes, or a low-rank delta gated by the score.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: An underfit G is a systematic capability failure across the bank. NNS-024 remains in force if the generator is just a shared template in disguise.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if ||G(h_e) - target_factors|| requires h_e or G large enough that embeddings+G exceed independent skinny factors. Kill if G emits dense W. Do not score this by pairwise cosine of W.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: G stored once; payload is h_e. Win only if dim(h_e)+|G| << E*|W|. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Token path identical to the emitted-factor kernel; G is bind-time. ns UNKNOWN on the token path by construction.
storage_candidates.mechanism: expert embeddings / generators: each expert is a small embedding h_e; a shared generator G maps h_e to the factors a kernel consumes (cores, codes, or skinny maps), not to a dense W_e.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: At bind time, G(h_e) emits C_e (or sparse codes) into the same buffers the small-core / dictionary kernel already consumes. The token path never calls G if cores are materialized as skinny factors; G is a storage generator, not a per-token network. Never emit dense W_e from G.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not NNS-024 procedural generated expert bases on orthogonal experts: this does not assume similarity and does not emit W. Not an unchanged archetype (h_e differs; G is shared).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: NNS-024 killed generated bases that buy bits BECAUSE experts are similar. A generator as a compressed parameterization can represent orthogonal experts if G is expressive; the embedding is identity, not a similarity exploit. Bytes live in G once plus E embeddings.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If XX^T energy at r is low, every expert loses the same complement (systematic). Gate/up historically break first. Gaussian X is a recorded artifact (NS-009 / NNS-001) and is forbidden as the falsifier's input.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: One layer, one organ, real X (never Gaussian). Uncoded V from activation PCA; reconstruct C_e (V x) vs W_e x. Kill if output cosine is no better than an orthogonal-V control at the r the byte plan needs. If uncoded already dies, quantizing C_e cannot save it. Do not run on a specimen in this lane.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Skinny payload scales as r/d_in of the expert mass plus amortized V. Algebraic identity only; magnitude UNKNOWN pending specimen.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One shared V @ x plus top-k skinny maps, vs top-k full matvecs. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: shared input transforms: one activation-space transform z = V @ x from the real residual stream (PCA / Hessian-weighted), then expert-specific skinny maps on z. Experts may be orthogonal as W and still share input covariance.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Compute z = V @ x once per layer (serves gate+up if they share V). Selected experts apply skinny C_e to z. Down: skinny then shared U. Lookup-free GEMM. Forbidden: materialize W_e = C_e V then qmm.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not trivial shared basis (activation-space V, not a shared weight basis plus residual on W). Not raw global similarity (does not use W cosine).
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: The surviving premise of the shared-basis packet: the residual stream is one vector. Weight-space tying is dead; sharing the transform of x does not require W cosine. This is SB1 in that packet, never fitted here, still untested on a Doctor path.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If experts need distinct output directions, a shared U smears them. Combining in latent is algebraically exact only when U is shared; a hybrid (clustered U) must not pretend otherwise.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if a shared U at the r that saves bytes cannot match per-expert expansions on a planted sandwich; then on one layer down_proj at a later stage. Kill if combine-in-latent disagrees with expand-then-sum by more than the combiner's linearity allows (it must be identical when U is fully shared).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Amortizes tall down expansion. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One expansion GEMV instead of top-k expansions. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: shared output latent spaces: each expert emits a small latent u_e; a shared U expands to d_model. Combine can happen in the latent. Dual of shared input transforms, on the output side.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Selected experts write u_e into an r-vector. Kernel does u = sum_e π_e u_e then y = U @ u, or y_e = U @ u_e if U is only partly shared. U is bound once. Never store or form W_down,e.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not a trivial shared basis (output-side only, combine-in-latent is part of the object). Not mean-expert subtraction.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: down_proj is the historically tolerant organ (hgravs01 live on Q80 down as a per-expert low-rank screen). Sharing the expansion U is the storage form of 'one output expansion' on the compute axis. Combine-in-latent is cheaper than expand-then-sum.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: A bad predictor adds a residual as large as the original factor (byte loss). Do not confuse a small W-cosine with a small factor residual; they are different measurements.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if residual energy of predicted factors is ~1 (then prediction is a no-op, matching the tying control). The test is on factors, not on flattened W. Do not reopen same-index W tying.
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Stores residual of predicted factors, not a second full bank. Win only if the residual is small. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Token path unchanged if residuals are fused at bind. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: cross-layer expert prediction: predict layer L+1's expert factors from layer L's (same index or learned map); store only the residual of that prediction. Weights are not tied.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Bind predictors P that map C_e,L -> C_e,L+1_hat as a small linear map on factors. Token path uses the residual-corrected factors already in the same skinny buffers. No dense W_L or W_{L+1}.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not same-index cross-layer weight tying (atlas / NNS-024). The stored object is a factor residual, not tied W.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Same-index WEIGHT tying is dead (control at 1e-7). Predicting a skinny core or code, and storing the residual, is a delta-code of factors, not a tie of W. Adjacent layers see related residual streams even when W cosine is ~0.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: If shared_op is the mean, this IS the dead noetic hypothesis. If residual is dense, bytes do not move. Capability dies when the residual cannot carry the expert's distinct function.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if ||residual_e|| / ||expert_e|| is ~1 on the named shared_op (mean-expert already showed this). The falsifier must name the shared_op; 'the mean' is not an allowed shared_op. Do not merge omitted experts from residuals (NNS-023).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Shared op stored once; per-expert payload is the residual. Win iff residual is small. Magnitude UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: One shared_op plus top-k skinny residuals. ns UNKNOWN.
storage_candidates.mechanism: conditional residuals: y = shared_op(x) + residual_e(x), where shared_op is a learned or architecture-native shared operator (not the mean expert) and residual_e is skinny / sparse / gated.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Compute y_shared = shared_op(x) once. Selected experts add R_e @ z (skinny) or a sparse residual. Sum. Never form W_e = W_shared + R_e as a dense matrix.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not shared-mean subtraction (explicitly forbidden as shared_op). Not expert merging. Not an unchanged archetype.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: Subtracting the mean expert leaves residual norm 0.984 (EXPERT_FAMILY_GENOME noetic REFUTED). A learned or native shared op (Flash/Qwen shared expert, or a fitted shared SwiGLU) can still leave a small residual even when the mean is useless. SB4 in the shared-basis packet is this idea for models that already have a shared expert; it was not fitted here.

storage_candidates.capability_risk: Wrong island labels mix a sensitive expert into a tolerant codec and fail capability first. Uniform sub-bit across islands is the dead lever this exists to avoid.
storage_candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Kill if island labels derived from a capability screen do not reduce per-island joint-SVD null-gap vs the global null (then the partition is cosmetic). Kill if the partition is used to justify a single codec family across organs (NNS-018).
storage_candidates.expected_byte_effect: Sharing confined to tolerant islands; sensitive islands may store independent. Net byte effect UNKNOWN and possibly small.
storage_candidates.expected_compute_effect: Per-island native paths; extra dispatch topology. ns UNKNOWN and possibly worse if islands fragment the wave.
storage_candidates.mechanism: capability-sensitive expert islands: partition the bank by capability / organ sensitivity (gate vs down, layer-band, tool vs language), and share structure only inside an island. Islands may use different mechanisms.
storage_candidates.native_execution_concept: Tag experts/organs with an island id. Each island binds its own shared factors and native path (e.g. down island uses shared U, gate island stays independent or uses a milder skinny). The kernel dispatches per island; it does not densify a mixed W.
storage_candidates.scar_distance: Not raw global similarity (partitioned on purpose). Not a single unconditioned shared basis across the bank.
storage_candidates.why_it_might_work: NS-uniform-subbit / NNS-018: organs do not fail together; a single family across gate/up/down is INSUFFICIENT. Sharing that ignores the split will re-kill on the sensitive organ. Islands make that split the partition, so sharing is only attempted where the organ is tolerant.
